title: Mars Helicopter Team’s Final Gathering for Ingenuity Data Downlink
description: B-roll for media and public use. On April 16, 2024, NASA’s Ingenuity team gathered in mission control at the agency’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory to celebrate the Mars helicopter’s accomplishments and complete one final “downlink poll,” a group opportunity to monitor a transmission from the helicopter. Ingenuity became the first vehicle to achieve powered, controlled flight on another planet when it took to the Martian skies on April 19, 2021. It flew for the final time on Jan. 18, 2024.  The following is a list of team members who appear in the Ingenuity commemoration video, in order of appearance:  ● Josh Anderson - Ingenuity Team Lead, JPL ● Martin Cacan - Ingenuity Chief Pilot, JPL ● Jaakko Karras - Ingenuity Chief Engineer Emeritus, JPL ● Harel Dor - Ingenuity Deputy Operations Lead, JPL ● Dave Lavery - Ingenuity Program Executive, NASA HQ ● Teddy Tzanetos - Ingenuity Project Manager, JPL  Though its flying days are over, Ingenuity’s computer and cameras are still functioning. So, while members of the helicopter team are moving on to other projects at JPL, Ingenuity has been programmed to take additional images and temperature measurements and transmit them to the nearby Mars Perseverance rover for as long as it can. After the rover goes out of communications range, the data will be recorded in the helicopter’s onboard memory.  Engineers hope to get additional data to characterize the ongoing performance of the helicopter’s various components.  Designed to be a technology demonstration that would make no more than five test flights in 30 days, Ingenuity far surpassed expectations, soaring higher and faster than previously imagined and eventually completing 72 flights.  For more information on Ingenuity, visit: go.nasa.gov/ingenuity.  Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech
